reviews.comment: bets prof ever
He's awesome so far, I really like him

Good lecturer and explains topics clearly. Publishes uncompleted notes on canvas but fills them out in lecture so attendance is somewhat necessary. Weekly homeworks take about 2-3 hours each. Quizzes every other week and three exams (including final), all about the same difficulty as the homework. Problems are graded based on work done.

Best professor I've ever had. Lectures are amazing, notes are super clear, and his explanations always make sense. Hw is reasonable and prepares you a lot for the exams and quizzes. He also gives you a bunch of practice problems to study for the exam. He's always willing to help and answer any questions. Also just a really kind and chill guy.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great prof. Lectures are useful. Homework's can be lengthy and time-consuming. Exams are fair, and the final was a bit easier than the midterms.

Genuinely the best professor I've had. He is a little shy but super nice and chill and funny. Always has the best answers and explanations for questions. His notes are very clear and easy to follow. Hw is pretty reasonable. He gives you the answer to the hw questions so you're graded on work. Exams are similar to hw. My goat, he's amazing

Super chill, awesome, fun guy. His lectures are clear and he is always willing to answer questions. He's also very responsive with emails. The homework is reasonable and helps you learn the material. The quizzes and exams are exactly like the homework, so review those to do well.
His explanations just seemed to always click at the end. Easily the best diff eq prof out there
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Thicke is a phenomenal professor who explains things well. The class format and expectations were clear, and the exam material did not try to trick you at all. I highly recommend
Final was light work and he's awesome

Dr. Thicke is incredible. I have never had a professor so excellent at explaining concepts until I took this class. He is the epitome of a good professor. Super kind, funny, helpful, and accessible outside of class. He's such a cutie patootie too. I feel sad knowing that I won't have him as a professor again.

Best professor I've ever had. He explains the content super well. Every time he explains something, he tells us WHY we do this method and why we even need to know it. Answers questions pretty well. I don't think he means to be, but he's super funny. Homework takes a while, but prepares you well for quizzes and exams.
Absolute goat. Amazing lectures, organized notes, very smart, clears up any confusion you have. Exams are similar to hw and practice problems. I wish I could take him for every class.
Exam heavy being worth around 80 percent of the exam, 30 percent final and 25 percent each midterm. Quiz are almost the same as HW. AMZInG. Easy to self study.
AMAZING!!!!!!
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He's a cutie

Exams are fair. They're pretty much like the homework and he posts a bunch of practice problems for you to do to study for the exam. His notes are super clear and he breaks down each and every step when working through examples during lectures. There's 5 quizzes and it's just two questions that are very similar to what you did on homework/notes.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a great lecturer and makes everything very clear and easy to understand. Also, just a great guy, super nice, kind of awkward lol but in a good way, and really knows what he's talking about. One of the best professors I've ever taken. If you can, definetely take his class.

Genuinely the BEST professor I have ever had bro. His lectures are so easy to understand because he's just so good at explaining everything and his tests and quizzes are similar to the homework. He's very fair and understanding as well!
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Thicke explains topics very well. The lectures are well structured and if you actually listen, homework, and exams become manageable. I got to learn a lot from his written and programming assignments, and have added a dimension of thinking whenever I look at a data science problem statement.

Explains differential equations and the mechanisms behind the class very well. 308 is very practical and is often taught to students as a "toolbox," but it doesn't give any good understanding of how the tools actually work. Dr. Thicke makes sure you actually understand your tools. First exam might hit a little hard though!
Prof. Thicke made Diff eq. so easy he explains things extremely well. By far the best math professor I've ever had.

Best prof I've had at A&M by far. His lectures are always structured really well, so it makes clear sense why we're learning what we are. Fair grader, for MATH 677 he gave the answers for homework (though he made the tests hard to compensate) because he believed homework should serve as practice.

Had Thicke in Fall 23. He is an outstanding prof for math since he uses a tablet and works through his lecture material every step of the way with his students. His work is clear and concise as well as when he's answering questions before, during, and after class. Everything you need to succeed in this course he has and can give. Highly recommend.

Dr. Thicke is a great 308 prof. His notes are very detailed, and his exams are very similar to the classwork. He is very quick to respond (all emails I have sent him are responded to within 2 hours, even on weekends!) Take him for this course.

While he explains everything very well he does tend to be a bit monotone so the class is not very engaging. What I do love about him is that he puts out note sheets before the lecture so you can follow along easily. He was always very polite and ready to answer questions, definitely one of the better math department professors.

Great Professor! Homework is tedious and much harder than the actual exam. Exams are very straightforward and much partial credit is given. My only complaint is that he might be a little monotone and his classes are taught at a slow pace. He is very accessible, and understanding, and responds quickly to emails. Would definitely recommend him.

Very boring lecturer, impossible to stay awake and actually learn something because he speaks so monotonously and quietly.  Tests were alright, usually stayed fairly close to review material.  Notes were sometimes hard to follow but had most of what you needed.  SO MUCH HOMEWORK: way too many textbook problems to be reasonable, many hours per week.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would take Thicke if you can for Cal 1. If you took AP Calc in high school, I can say that you can pretty much skip every class after vectors and get As on all of the tests. The practice tests online are very helpful, and the class is structured well. Thicke is monotone, but is very knowledgeable in math and helpful.

Thicke is a very good professor and a decent lecturer. His office hours are very helpful and he is always willing to answer a question asked of him. I had him for Math 151 and the assignments and exams are common to all other sections.

Not a perfect lecturer but he certainly checks all the boxes and gets the job done. Gives a ton of resources: lecture notes, common exams, weekly help sessions, office hours, and more. You could get an A in this class without showing up to a single lecture; just use lecture notes and online resources such as common exams to study.
reviews.ratingTags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super nice but very reserved, however, as you get further along in the semester you figure out his humor and he's such a funny guy. Lectures are good and notes are posted. If you have never taken cal before this class will be difficult but study and ask questions and you will be fine. STUDY for the exams and take practice tests, 80% of grade!!!

Professor Thicke was an incredibly nice professor and could be very entertaining. He is really reserved but is very knowledgeable in his subject. If you don't have previous knowledge of calculus or python, get a tutor before it's too late. Notes are set up well and he does post them. which is very helpful.

Thicke is a good professor. He is overall a good lecturer who gets his point across. Sometimes he doesn't explain the steps that he takes in example problems very well, but he will elaborate nicely if you just ask him what he did. He does a lot of redundant examples but it can be helpful for confusing topics.

Most of the quizzes, labs, and homeworks are very easy, however one of the FRQ questions on every test was unusually difficult and unlike any practice problem we had ever seen or gone over. Tests are also worth 80% of your grade so make sure you know what you are doing before test days.
The BEST prof you can ask for MATH 151. He is caring, kind and very reserved. The classes can be quiet sometimes but if listen to the lectures and take notes you should be fine.

Kyle is a very good professor who is very knowledgeable about calculus. His lectures can be monotone, but he is very kind and accessible for his students. There are four exams, with the first three being common exams not written by Kyle. The final is his test. Overall not super difficult for veteran calculus students.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing math professor. Explained everything well and was always available outside of class. Very caring and kind. If you pay attention in lecture you will do well. Do the homework, ask for help, ask questions he will help with all of it. Fair grader and also just a really awesome person to have as a math teacher.  Highly recommend! 11/10

Professor Thicke is great, super straight to the point but really makes you understand what's going on. He'll practice new concepts over and over, making each step super clear and answering questions on the way. The complaints about him being quiet only really apply in the beginning of the year or if the class is being loud. Would highly recommend.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Thicke is excellent at teaching the content, for he shows us the "why" behind concepts to help build our intuition. He's also a very nice and chill guy - very approachable if you need help. Although his lectures aren't the most entertaining, you'll do great if you pay attention and  actively take notes.

Professor Thicke was a great professor for Math 151. Although I already know most of the topics covered (other than vectors), attending his lecture was very insightful, as he would always explain the proofs for the theorems that were used in lecture. I always would walk out of the lecture hall with a better understanding of what was taught that day

Prof Thicke might be the most driest, yet funniest lecturer I have ever had. He's a solid teacher for calc 1 and a safe bet if you need an easy A. I came into the course with a strong background in calc 1, but even if i didn't, he did a great job of teaching the material.

Great lecturer, along with the TAs. Can be a little dull, but he is very knowledgeable and obviously passionate about the subject. Will answer questions thoroughly whenever asked. The course is almost entirely exam-based, with 3 Exams and a Final exam all forming 80% of your final grade. Exams are sort of difficult but easy to prepare for.

I really liked his lectures. He was kinda quiet, but lectures were very informative. He was very receptive to questions asked, and was very happy to answer them. He's pretty nice, and you can tell he really likes math. For tests, he provides links to past exams, and weekly reviews, making it easy to study. He was a really great teacher overall.

My grade is what it is because of me, not him. You can easily reach him through email, office hours, or after/before class. He very clearly explains whatever concepts you ask about. He is very passionate about math! It's fun seeing him skittish like a scared weasel (in a good way) and then smiling ear to ear the next. He's quiet, but very good.

I truly enjoyed his lectures when I went to them. He is a very good teacher and the overall test scores reflect that. This year saw 151 made into a weed out class, which made the class much harder. I think he is a great professor, just a bit quiet.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are kind of quiet and boring but is very useful and thorough. You can tell he loves math. Weekly homeworks can be difficult but he has lots of office hour availability and is always willing to help out.

Very kind and prepared, long weekly homeworks but mostly completion. 2 exams and one final. Understood when tests were too hard and made up for it. Explained everything thoroughly during lecture but VERY quiet and monotone. As long as you pay attention during lecture and put effort into the homework you should be fine.

Dr. Thicke is a great professor. While he is a bit quiet during lectures he thoroughly explains each topic and does plenty of example problems. There is a lot of homework assigned each week, usually consisting of many textbook problems, so be prepared. The 2 exams and final weren't very difficult as long as you studied. Take him for Diffeq!
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
You could definitely do a lot worse than professor Thicke. I think he strikes a good balance between explaining what we are doing (proofs/concepts) and how to do it (solving the problem). Despite it being his first year teaching, he did a good job. 
Also, he's kind of shy.

Prof. Thicke is great at teaching differential equations. Diff eq. is hard and the notes and homeworks are too, but he provides great resources to succeed and tests are not overly difficult, in my opinion, though you may want to know definitions of functions and other rules which caught me off guard on my first exam. Also highly recommend Xournal++
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Kyle Thicke is very kind and smart. However, I didn't learn well from his lectures because he speaks so quietly and they're a bit confusing. Most of the exam is free response, and I'd fully work out problems yet receive 0/12 on most questions as soon as I made one mistake, there isn't much partial credit given. Not the worst but hard very grader.

Dr. Thicke isn't the most confident lecturer, but his handwriting is clear, so there were no problems understanding lectures. He explains concepts well and frequently pauses for questions. Lectures were a bit slow in my opinion and very example heavy, but he thoroughly covered everything that could be seen on an exam so there were no surprises.

Tests are graded pretty easy and are multiple-choice/free answer. Uses WebAssign homework, which is usually trickier than the tests and quizzes. Quizzes are weekly and open-note. Doesn't do a super great job explaining clearly in lectures, but will answer questions if you ask. Recommended using math learning center resources in addition to class.

Very good prof. Good at listening to students and providing understandable responses. Was understanding for any issues I personally had, and happened to ride the same bus to his early class. Very smart, very personable, easily one of my favorite math professors. YOU MUST study for exams however, they are not easy.

Nice guy but was a little shy during lectures. Other than him being shy, he was really good. Taught the material well and was helpful with questions. There is a good amount of homework but it is more than manageble.

Professor Thicke's lectures were thorough and he gave plenty of examples. Before each test, he posts a previous exam and its key, allowing us to see what kind of questions will be asked. Very good prof overall

Thicke is a great professor who wants to see his students succeed. He can be hard to listen to, yet he is knowledgeable and explains the topics well. If you go to class, you will be okay. Do not hesitate to ask him for help before or after class or during office hours.

Despite being brand new to Texas A&M, Professor Thicke is an amazing lecturer. His teaching makes perfect sense and is beyond helpful in understanding the material. One of the best math professors I've had, and many students from other classes came to his review sessions for help.

He gets grades in relatively quickly and makes sure you have a clear idea of the grading system and what to expect on the tests. His lectures are helpful and the homework he assigns helps a lot with the exams. He is pretty understanding and tries to help with questions and concerns students may have.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Thicke is easily the best math teacher I have ever had. He does an incredible job explaining the course concepts in a clear and concise manner, while also not rushing through. He actually makes the lectures enjoyable. The amount of homework is fair, and the homework problems are usually harder than the exam problems. I highly recommend Thicke.

Thicke is a good professor that keeps his lectures very well paced. Of all the math classes that I've taken at TAMU, this one has felt the least rushed. He does well explaining concepts and how they are useful for real life applications. I would definitely recommend him.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Thicke is by far one of the best professors I have ever had. His lectures are clear, concise, and easy to understand, he offers plenty of alternative study resources out of class, and he will overlook basically every mistake on the exams if you show that you understand the core ideas. Thicke makes multivariable calculus feel like a walk in the park
Very good professor, doesn't test concepts super in depth and doesn't make questions unnecessarily complicated/difficult. Very good professor for MATH 251

Professor Thicke posts the best notes on Canvas and they explain all the concepts very clearly. I went to lectures very rarely because of this, but the ones I went to he went into more detail about everything on his notes. It's very possible to get an A without going to a single lecture. Overall, the class is mid, but the prof is absolutely GOATED.

Prof Thicke is probably one of the best MATH 251 profs out there. His class is so straightforward and as long as you do the quizzes and assignments there is virtually no way you can fail this class even if you skip some lectures.

Kyle made the lectures enjoyable and easy to understand. He provides lots of study material for tests and does the Week-In-Review sessions, so the questions are exactly like the ones on his tests. Although the subject is difficult, he makes it an easy class to pass.
Awesome. Take him for 251 or any other math class. Your search for teachers is over.
Take him at all costs. He is the GOAT

Calc 3 isn't meant to be easy, but Kyle makes it as close to easy as possible. The tests are basically just like the homework. Just make sure you have a few people you can study with since cengage won't tell you what you're doing wrong and everyone has dropped a negative or two.

Thicke is the goat math professor. Everything he explains in class is clear and concise. Plus he does the week-in-review which are nearly identical to his exams. I would take him again in a heartbeat.
